title: Timing strategy performance in the crude oil futures market
summary: Volatility-timing utility evidence is not a net CL strategy result. Source warm-up, overnight treatment and cost units block direct testing.
about: Decomposing crude-oil timing benefits into forecastable return moments.
findings: Authors attribute most utility gains to volatility forecasting. Tables3–4 report certainty-equivalent utility, not realized account profits; higher odd-moment forecasts require unrealistic skill.
mechanism: Changing exposure with predictable risk can improve utility; no new independently verified directional alpha.
build_on: Keep as risk-method context. Owned CL begins2017, so source1000-day warm-up for full2018 design is not admitted. Source removes overnight price differences.
can_strategy_code_be_made: A model can be coded after source/units/session reconciliation; no shortened warm-up, omitted risk or CER-to-cash conversion is authorized.
reading_scope: Selected primary31-page working-paper introduction, definitions, data,1000-day estimation setting and Tables2–4; not full paper.
source_version: Nick Taylor2017 working paper: wrapper2March2017, internal cover15March2017. Accepted-manuscript parity unconfirmed.
owned_input_mapping: Owned CL minute fields overlap raw inputs, but source1988–2015 history, fitting warm-up and return/session construction do not match the design panel.
deeper_investigation: No current return test. Retain measurement lessons; do not turn an ineligible risk-method illustration into a portfolio candidate.
cost_caution: Source tau=4e-4 must be reconciled to its strategy interval and native CL fills before interpreting it as a round-trip cost.
